title: TypeNet: Deep Learning Keystroke Biometrics
abstract: The paper investigates LSTM networks for keystroke biometric authentication in free-text scenarios, comparing three learning approaches (softmax, contrastive, triplet loss) and evaluating performance across physical/touchscreen keyboards. TypeNet achieves EER of 2.2% and 9.2% for physical and touchscreen keyboards, respectively, outperforming prior methods.
problem_statement: High intra-class variability in free-text keystroke biometrics and scalability challenges for large-scale Internet authentication.
methodology: LSTM-based deep learning models trained with keystroke sequences, evaluated using different loss functions, sample sizes, and device types (physical vs touchscreen keyboards).
dataset: Largest free-text keystroke databases with >136M keystrokes from 168,000 physical keyboard users and 60,000 touchscreen users.
performance: TypeNet achieves 2.2% EER for physical keyboards and 9.2% for touchscreen keyboards, with scalable performance up to 100,000 users.
contribution: Introduces TypeNet, a scalable LSTM model for free-text keystroke authentication; achieves state-of-the-art results; provides cross-device and cross-database generalization.
limitations: Performance degrades with very large user counts; device-specific behavior may affect accuracy.
future_work: Explore hybrid models for multi-device authentication, improve robustness to environmental variations, and expand to other behavioral biometrics.

title: Covert lie detection using keyboard dynamics
abstract: Identifying the true identity of a subject in the absence of external verification criteria is an unresolved issue. Here, we report an experiment on the verification of fake identities using keystroke dynamics, achieving ~95% accuracy by analyzing typing patterns with unexpected questions.
problem_statement: Detecting fake identities without external verification (documents, biometrics) in security and online contexts.
methodology: Keystroke dynamics analysis using unexpected questions to reveal deception clues through typing pattern deviations.
dataset: 60 participants (40 training, 20 test) with fabricated ID profiles and real personal information.
performance: Achieved 95% accuracy in distinguishing liars from truth-tellers using keystroke dynamics.
contribution: Novel covert lie detection method using keyboard dynamics instead of mouse tracking for online applications.
limitations: Requires predefined questions; generalizability to real-world scenarios may be limited.
future_work: Explore real-world deployment and integration with other biometric modalities.

title: Non-Acted Text and Keystrokes Database and Learning Methods to Recognize Emotions
abstract: This work presents a multimodal text-keystrokes dataset and learning methods for emotion recognition. A dataset of 69 participants is collected across scenarios, with stimuli induced via videos. Text and keystroke features are extracted and fused to achieve 86.95% accuracy in emotion classification, with 100% accuracy for pleasure-displeasure classes using SVM and feature fusion.
problem_statement: Identifying dominant emotions from text and keystroke data is critical for human-computer interaction, requiring robust multimodal analysis methods.
methodology: Text-keystroke data is collected from 69 participants via controlled video stimuli. Features are extracted from text and keystrokes, fused with tree-based selection and SVM for emotion classification.
dataset: Multimodal text-keystrokes dataset with 69 participants, including video-induced stimuli and unguided text reviews.
performance: 86.95% accuracy via text-keystroke fusion; 100% accuracy for pleasure-displeasure classes using SVM and feature fusion.
contribution: Introduces a novel CI-based framework and baseline dataset for emotion recognition in short text, combining text and keystroke features.
limitations: Data collected in controlled environments may lack real-world variability; limited to predefined emotion classes.
future_work: Expand datasets to include diverse scenarios, explore real-time emotion detection, and integrate multimodal data streams.
model_type: Supervised learning with SVM, discriminant analysis, and k-NN classifiers

title: The Influence of Emotion on Keyboard Typing: An Experimental Study Using Auditory Stimuli
abstract: The study investigates how emotions affect keyboard typing patterns using auditory stimuli. Keystroke dynamics were analyzed via two-way Valence x Arousal ANOVA, revealing significant effects of arousal on duration and latency but not accuracy.
problem_statement: Limited prior research on emotion-induced variance in keyboard typing patterns necessitated this study to explore emotional influences on keystroke dynamics.
methodology: Controlled experiment using International Affective Digitized Sounds (IADS) to induce emotional states, followed by two-way ANOVA analysis of keystroke data.
dataset: Keystroke data collected from 52 participants under IADS-induced emotional conditions (Valence x Arousal dimensions).
performance: Arousal significantly affected duration (p < .05) and latency (p < .01), but not accuracy. Emotional effects were smaller than individual variability.
contribution: Demonstrates arousal influences keystroke duration/latency, suggesting personalized models could enhance emotion recognition accuracy.
limitations: Small emotional effect size and potential methodological limitations in parameter specificity.
future_work: Explore personalized models for emotion recognition and deeper analysis of emotional state interactions.
model_type: Traditional statistical methods (ANOVA) and machine learning algorithms

title: DeepMood: Modeling Mobile Phone Typing Dynamics for Mood Detection
abstract: The increasing use of electronic communication presents opportunities to study mental health via mobile phone metadata. A pilot study explores bipolar disorder connections with phone usage, proposing DeepMood, an end-to-end deep architecture for mood prediction using typing dynamics metadata with 90.31% depression score accuracy.
problem_statement: Detect mood disturbances and severity using mobile phone typing dynamics metadata, offering non-intrusive mental health monitoring in daily life settings.
methodology: Proposes DeepMood, a late fusion deep architecture combining RNNs for multi-view metadata (keypress timing, accelerometer) with interaction modeling across views.
dataset: BiAffect study data from 20 participants (7 bipolar I, 5 bipolar II, 8 controls) with session-level typing metadata and clinical ratings (HDRS/YMRS).
performance: Achieved 90.31% depression score prediction accuracy using session-level typing dynamics (typically <1 minute), demonstrating feasibility of metadata-driven mood inference.
contribution: 1) Data analysis linking typing patterns to bipolar mood states; 2) Novel two-stage late fusion strategy for multi-view time series; 3) Empirical validation of mobile metadata for mood prediction.
limitations: Privacy constraints limit character data collection; reliance on self-reported clinical ratings may introduce bias; requires further validation on diverse populations.
future_work: Expand dataset diversity, improve real-time monitoring, integrate multimodal data, and validate in clinical settings.
model_type: Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) with late fusion
